newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CLEMENTE UNDER FIRE FOR OLYMPIC 'DIDN'T TRY' COMMENTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CLEMENTE UNDER FIRE FOR OLYMPIC 'DIDN'T TRY' COMMENTS.

text.p: Controversial Spanish coach Javier Clemente has walked into another barrage of criticism after claiming he did not train the country's under-23 side with a view to retaining their Olympic title in Atlanta.
"I didn't prepare the Olympic team to win; the players are above the result, and I couldn't burn them out," said Clemente, whose team crashed out 4-0 to Argentina in the quarter-finals.
Clemente was criticised at the time for picking only under-21 players, and refusing to use the three senior players allowed in the tournament.
The protests were nothing new for a man who seems to enjoy withstanding heavy media fire.
His latest remarks were made at a news conference ahead of Wednesday's World Cup qualifier with Slovakia, have subsequently excited the wrath of the Spanish sporting establishment.

"The Olympic side doesn't seem like much to him; perhaps the Football Federation ought to look for another coach for the team," said Alfredo Goyoeneche, vice-president of the Spanish Olympic Commitee.
Atletico Madrid midfielder Diego Simeone, who played in the Argentine Olympic side, was also criticial.
"Now he's looking for a load of excuses...the Spanish players didn't go to sunbathe," said Simeone.
Journalists have used the remarks as a pretext to renew their war of words with the Basque coach.
"He gave a surprising exhibition of Olympic spirit when he said he didn't take the team to Atlanta to win, but only to participate," joked a columnist in the sports daily As.
Clemente can hardly be accused of playing to the gallery in his relationship with the press.
"Nothing of what you say affects me...It's not that some of you are wrong in your judgment, it's that you don't have judgment for anything," he told reporters on Tuesday.

In one celebrated incident, Clemente was deemed responsible for pinning a sheet of complaints against journalists in the interior of the plane that brought both the Spanish team and reporters back from a World Cup game in Prague.
Such is the controversy generated by the coach that the pro or anti-Clemente stances of Spanish newspapers and radio stations are well known in the country.
But Clemente has gone some way to correcting some of his gravest faults in the public eye.
Veteran striker Julio Salinas, a fellow Basque, has disappeared from Clemente line-ups to the relief of millions of fans, while the clamour for Raul Gonzalez has finally been answered.
The Real Madrid teenager is living up to the expectation, and led Spain to an impressive 4-1 victory over Slovakia.
Even so Clemente's enemies were sharpening their knives after the coach had scrapped the traditional pre-match video session, and confessed that he knew little about the opponents.
"Clemente ought to give back what he earns," said Atletico Madrid coach Radomir Antic, a long-time sparring partner "It's shameful that the Spanish coach hadn't seen Slovakia play away."
